passage:
A store asked customers whether they wanted paper or digital receipts. Digital receipts saved paper, but required an email or phone number.
Some customers chose paper because they did not want more messages. Others chose digital and later received advertisements.
A consumer class discussed the trade-off. Saving paper was good, but personal data also had value.
The store later changed its system: customers could choose a digital receipt without joining marketing lists.
The receipt seemed like a small choice, but it involved privacy, waste, and business.
Modern convenience often asks for information. People should know what they are giving when they choose it.

questions.stem: Which title is best for the complete passage that includes “A store asked customers whether they wanted paper or digital receipts.”?

本文可直接核對「The Digital Receipt: A store asked customers whether they wanted paper or digital receipts.」，所以這個選項符合完整語境。
本文沒有陳述「The Digital Divide」；這個選項混入另一個情境的資訊。
本文沒有陳述「The Digital Ticket」；這個選項混入另一個情境的資訊。
